narrative:

This placed you far outside the range associated with bar success, and it moved the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing also pointed in the same direction: the second decile versus the sixth decile average among admitted students. It was the second most important reason for the decision, reinforcing the picture of consistently low grades. Less influential but still relevant, your LSAT score of 31 is well below the admitted pool's average of 37.18, contributing a further, more moderate push toward a predicted failure.

Taken together, these three signals outweighed the strengths of your application. To improve your prospects, focus on raising your class standing in subsequent years, retake the LSAT with preparation, and build a record of strong academic performance before reapplying.
